summary: Paul's testimony in Galatians 1:11-24 shows how God took a well-educated, zealous persecutor of the church and turned him into one of Christianity's greatest missionaries. Steve draws three points from it: Jesus calls each of us to follow Him regardless of our past, God equips us for what He calls us to (sometimes immediately and supernaturally, sometimes through the wisdom our own past mistakes and experience give us), and before we can share the gospel with others we need to know it and believe it ourselves, confidently and without wavering. The sermon closes with a challenge to be as bold about our faith as we are about anything else we're passionate about, and to see each person's unique background as equipping them to reach people no one else can.
takeaways: Your past -- even a shameful one -- doesn't disqualify you from God's calling; Paul was actively persecuting the church before his conversion, and God used that same background to reach people others couldn't.
God equips people two ways: immediately and supernaturally (like Paul on the road to Damascus) and through wisdom earned the hard way over time -- both are real equipping, neither is lesser.
You can't share the gospel confidently until you know it well enough to recognize when something taught is off -- like the Bereans, who checked everything against Scripture.

Each believer has a unique sphere of influence -- people they alone are positioned to reach - and that's not incidental, it's part of how God builds His church. Real conviction shows: Steve's charge is to be as vocal about Christ as people are about CrossFit or veganism -- if believers spoke about Jesus with that same enthusiasm, it would be obvious.
